html:
The Battle of Blood River was fought on 16 December 1838 in what is now KwaZulu-Natal, where about 470 Voortrekkers under Andries Pretorius defeated a Zulu army of the king Dingane.

The trekkers, who had come in the Great Trek, formed their wagons into a laager beside the Ncome river and fired on the attacking regiments with muskets and two small cannon. Some 3,000 Zulu were killed, and the river was said to run red, while only three trekkers were wounded.

Before the battle the trekkers swore a vow to keep the day holy if God gave them victory. The Day of the Vow became a sacred holiday of Afrikaner nationalism and of the apartheid state. Since 1994 the date has been the Day of Reconciliation, and a Zulu memorial stands across the river, beside the old Zulu kingdom.
sum: The Battle of Blood River was fought on 16 December 1838 in what is now KwaZulu-Natal, where about 470 Voortrekkers under Andries Pretorius defeated a Zulu army of the king Dingane.
